question: The server refuses to start with 'exactly one active key is required' or 'kid ... does not match its key'. What happened and how do you recover?
answer_hinglish:
Dono errors FileKeyRing.open() se aate hain jab keys.json load hota hai. Har stored key ka PEM parse hota hai aur uska RFC 7638 thumbprint nikalta hai; agar file ka 'kid' field us thumbprint se alag hai toh 'does not match its key' -- matlab kisi ne file haath se edit ki, do keys ke fields mix ho gaye, ya file corrupt hai. Doosra check: state activatedAt/retiredAt se derive hoti hai (activatedAt null = next, activatedAt set aur retiredAt null = active, dono set = retired), aur exactly ek active honi chahiye -- zero ya do active hon toh start fail. keys.test.ts dono cases test karta hai.

Kyun fail-fast? Galat key ring par chalna matlab ya toh kisi galat key se sign karna ya /jwks mein galat public keys -- dono silent bugs. Start fail hona saaf signal hai.

Recovery: (1) Backup se keys.json restore karo (agar hai). (2) Agar edit ki thi, toh 'kid' ko khaali ya sahi thumbprint karo aur exactly ek key ka retiredAt null + activatedAt set rakho. (3) Last resort: keys.json delete -- nayi active + next keys generate hongi, lekin purani keys se sign hue tokens (max 300 s) invalid ho jaayenge. File hamesha temp + rename se likhi jaati hai, toh crash se aadhi file normally nahi banti.
why_needed: Operators ko pata hona chahiye ki startup error ka matlab kya hai aur data kho diye bina kaise nikalna hai.
real_world_analogy: Chaabiyon ke guchhe par tag galat chipka hai: chowkidar maana kar deta hai, galat darwaza kholne ki jagah.
how_it_works: open: parse JSON -> per key signingKeyFromPem -> kid compare -> count active -> throw or construct.
in_this_project: src/keys.ts FileKeyRing.open; test/keys.test.ts 'a file with two active keys, or a kid that does not match its key, is refused'.
disadvantages: Recovery manual hai; koi repair tool nahi
common_mistakes: keys.json delete karke soch lena kuch nahi tootega
kid ko apni marzi ka naam dena
follow_up_questions: Keys ka backup kaise aur kahan rakhoge?
Repair CLI ka design kya hoga?

question: Why is signing behind a KeyRing interface with two implementations, StaticKeyRing and FileKeyRing? How does server.ts use it?
answer_hinglish:
KeyRing ke sirf do methods hain: signing(nowMs) -- abhi kaunsi key sign kare, aur published(nowMs) -- kaunsi keys /jwks mein hain aur verification ke liye accept hoti hain. server.ts ko rotation, files ya states ka kuch pata nahi; woh sendTokens mein ctx.ring.signing(ctx.now()) aur /jwks, /userinfo, /logout mein ctx.ring.published(ctx.now()) bulata hai.

StaticKeyRing stage 1 ka behaviour hai: fixed list, pehli key sign karti hai, sab published, kuch rotate nahi hota. Tests (startServer default) aur bina DATA_DIR wala CLI (SIGNING_KEY_FILE ya generated key) yahi use karte hain, toh stage 1 ke 125 tests bina badle chalte rahe. FileKeyRing stage 2 ka hai: keys.json, next/active/retired, auto-rotation.

nowMs parameter kyun? Clock injection: tests clock.t aage badha ke rotation, retention aur expiry bina sleep ke test karte hain -- wahi pattern jo server ke now() option mein hai. Interface ke peeche hone se aage KMS-backed ring (sign remote) ya shared ring (database) bina server.ts badle aa sakte hain. AuthServerOptions mein keyRing option keys se priority leta hai.
why_needed: Small interfaces seams banate hain: testing aasaan, aur implementation badalna local.
real_world_analogy: Bijli ka socket: aap generator lagao ya grid, appliance ko farak nahi padta.
how_it_works: createAuthHandler: ring = opts.keyRing ?? new StaticKeyRing(keys ?? [generateSigningKey()]).
in_this_project: src/keys.ts KeyRing, StaticKeyRing, FileKeyRing; src/server.ts createAuthHandler, sendTokens; src/index.ts.
disadvantages: Interface sync hai; remote KMS async hoga -- interface badalna padega
common_mistakes: Rotation logic server.ts mein likhna
Date.now() seedha key ring ke andar (untestable)
follow_up_questions: KMS ke liye async interface kaisa hoga?
Verification keys aur published keys alag hone chahiye kabhi?

question: A user says: 'I logged out in my laptop browser but my phone app is still signed in.' Is that a bug in this server?
answer_hinglish:
Nahi, yeh designed behaviour hai, lekin samjhana zaroori hai. Har successful login ek alag LoginSession (alag sid) banata hai, aur us login ke code se bani token family us sid se judi hai. /logout id_token_hint ke sid wali session khatam karta hai, plus browser cookie wali session agar woh same user (sub) ki hai. Phone app ka login alag session hai -- uska sid alag, cookie alag device par. Toh uski families revoke nahi hoti. Test 'only the families of THAT session are revoked; another login of the same user is untouched' isi ko lock karta hai.

Kya kuch aur ho sakta hai? Check karo: (1) Laptop par logout request 200/302 aayi ya 400 (galat post_logout_redirect_uri, missing hint, retired key se sign hua hint) -- 400 par kuch revoke nahi hota. (2) Laptop wale RP ne apni local session bhi clear ki? Hamara server sirf apni taraf ki cheezein khatam karta hai. (3) Access tokens offline verify karne wali APIs 300 s tak purana token maanengi.

Agar product ko 'log out everywhere' chahiye, toh woh NOT implemented hai (README): saari sessions of a sub + unki families revoke, aur doosre RPs ko back-channel logout. Yeh feature request hai, bug nahi.
why_needed: Support tickets mein 'expected vs actual' samajhna debugging ka pehla step hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ki ek chaabi lautane se doosri chaabi (jo phone ke paas hai) band nahi hoti.
how_it_works: logout: ended = {hint.sid} + same-sub cookie session; other sids untouched.
in_this_project: src/server.ts handleLogout; test/logout.test.ts; README NOT implemented ('log out everywhere').
advantages: Ek device ka logout doosre ko nahi todta
disadvantages: Global logout nahi
common_mistakes: Bug maan ke saari sessions revoke kar dena bina product decision ke
follow_up_questions: 'Log out everywhere' ka API kaisa hoga?
Back-channel logout isme kya jodta hai?

question: In handleLogout, every validation happens before any session is deleted or family revoked. Point to the lines and explain why an invalid logout request must have no side effects.
answer_hinglish:
handleLogout ka flow: (1) params parse (GET query ya POST form, repeated params -> 400). (2) id_token_hint missing -> 400. (3) aud unverified decode -> findClient -> unknown -> 400. (4) verifyJwt with ignoreExpiry -> fail -> 400 'id_token_hint is not valid (...)'. (5) client_id param mismatch -> 400. (6) post_logout_redirect_uri registered nahi -> 400. Sirf in sab ke BAAD: ended set banta hai, sessions.delete aur revokeFamily, phir cookie clear aur redirect/page.

Kyun? Agar koi invalid request bhi session khatam kar deti, toh: galat post_logout_redirect_uri wala attacker link bhi user ko logout kar deta (aur error page dikhata); forged hint (bina valid signature) se kisi ki session marti; ya ek client doosre client ke aud wale hint ke saath logout karwata. Rule: authenticate aur authorize poora karo, phir state badlo -- 'validate-then-commit', jaise refreshGrant mein scope check markUsed se pehle.

Tests yeh assert karte hain: har 400 case (5 URI variants, missing hint, tampered, foreign key, access token as hint, repeated param) ke baad expectStillValid -- access token /userinfo par 200. URI variants mein set-cookie header bhi null hona chahiye. Mutation M30 aur M31 inhi se pakde gaye.
why_needed: State-changing endpoints par partial failure ke side effects hi aksar vulnerabilities hote hain.
real_world_analogy: Hotel checkout: bill aur ID verify hone ke baad hi kamra release hota hai, pehle nahi.
how_it_works: Validate (no writes) -> compute ended -> writes -> response.
in_this_project: src/server.ts handleLogout; test/logout.test.ts (expectStillValid after every 400).
advantages: Har 400 path tested for no side effects
disadvantages: Lamba function; order fragile
common_mistakes: Cookie pehle clear karna
Revoke pehle aur URI check baad mein
follow_up_questions: Is function ko kaise refactor karoge (validate step alag)?
GET logout ko CSRF ke nazariye se kaise dekhte ho?

question: The login session already expired (12 h) or was already deleted, and then the RP sends the user to /logout. What still happens, and why?
answer_hinglish:
Session record (LoginSession) ka expiresAt hai, aur session store se delete bhi ho sakta hai (pehla logout). Lekin token families ka link session record par nirbhar nahi: har TokenFamily khud sid field rakhti hai (code se copy hui). handleLogout ended set mein hint ka sid daalta hai chahe session record ho ya na ho, phir sessions.delete(sid) (missing par no-op -- memory aur file store dono) aur familiesOfSession(sid) ki har family revokeFamily.

Toh: expired session ke baad bhi logout us login ke refresh tokens maar deta hai -- jo zaroori hai, kyunki refresh token 14 din chalta hai jabki session 12 ghante. Dusri baar logout (same hint): session pehle hi gayi, families pehle hi revoked; file store revokeFamily sirf tab log karta hai jab family revoked nahi thi, toh koi extra record nahi; response phir bhi 200/302. Test 'a second logout with the same hint is harmless'.

Ek limit: hint verify hona chahiye. Agar hint ki signing key retention ke baad /jwks se hat gayi (300 s rotation ke baad), toh 'unknown kid' -> 400 aur kuch revoke nahi. Us case mein user ko naya id_token (refresh se) chahiye, ya RP /revoke se refresh token khatam kare.
why_needed: Logout idempotent aur robust hona chahiye; RPs retry karte hain.
real_world_analogy: Membership card expire ho gaya lekin cancel request phir bhi linked sub-cards band karti hai.
how_it_works: ended.add(claims.sid) -> sessions.delete (no-op if missing) -> familiesOfSession(sid) -> revokeFamily (skip if revoked in file store).
in_this_project: src/server.ts handleLogout; src/store.ts TokenFamily.sid, MemorySessionStore.delete; src/file-store.ts revokeFamily guard.
advantages: Expired session ke baad bhi tokens khatam
disadvantages: Retired key ke baad purana hint fail
common_mistakes: Family revoke ko session record ke existence par depend karna
Dusre logout par error dena
follow_up_questions: Hint key retention ko logout ke liye lamba karoge?
Logout ka audit log kya record kare?

question: What exactly do the jose interop tests prove, and what do they NOT prove?
answer_hinglish:
jose ek independent, widely used JOSE library hai. Tests: (1) createRemoteJWKSet hamare /jwks ko fetch karta hai, aur jwtVerify hamare access token ko issuer, audience, algorithms ES256 aur typ at+jwt ke saath accept karta hai; id_token bhi audience = client_id ke saath. Yeh prove karta hai: hamara ES256 signature format (raw r||s, ieee-p1363) sahi hai, JWK export sahi hai, header (alg, typ, kid) sahi hai, aur claims standard hain. (2) Tampered signature par JWSSignatureVerificationFailed, galat audience par JWTClaimValidationFailed -- yani jose actually check kar raha hai, test 'always pass' nahi. (3) Rotation test: rotation se pehle fetched cache naya token verify karta hai (pre-publish), purana bhi, aur retention ke baad JWKSNoMatchingKey.

Kya prove NAHI karta: (a) Hamara verifyJwt sahi hai -- woh apne unit/userinfo tests se hai, jose sirf hamare tokens verify karta hai. (b) Real network conditions (TLS, proxies) -- tests plain http 127.0.0.1 par. (c) jose ka behaviour har version mein same -- pinned devDependency 6.2.15. (d) Doosri libraries (Java, Go) -- sirf ek library. (e) Rotation test mein jose ka 30 s cooldown ek implementation detail hai jis par 'no refetch' claim tika hai; comment mein likha hai.
why_needed: Interop tests tabhi kaam ke hain jab pata ho woh kis cheez ka saboot hain.
real_world_analogy: Doosre shehar ke lab se blood test: report ek independent confirmation hai, lekin sirf usi test ki jo karwaya.
how_it_works: jose: remote JWKS fetch -> kid match -> ES256 verify -> claims check (iss, aud, typ, exp).
in_this_project: test/interop.test.ts jose describe blocks; package.json devDependencies jose 6.2.15.
disadvantages: Ek library, ek version, plain http
common_mistakes: Interop pass ko 'secure' ka saboot maan lena
Sirf positive interop tests
follow_up_questions: Doosri language ki library se interop kaise add karoge?
jose ke cooldown par test ka depend karna risky hai kya?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Ek mature library se interop sasta aur high-signal; zyada libraries = zyada confidence aur maintenance.
advanced.failure_scenarios: jose upgrade par cooldown default badle toh rotation test ka 'no refetch' assumption toot sakta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Conformance suite run, jose version matrix, TLS ke saath interop.

question: While writing the openid-client interop tests, which settings were needed (allowInsecureRequests, id_token_signed_response_alg, manual login form) and why is each one not a weakness of the server?
answer_hinglish:
openid-client v6 (oauth4webapi par bana) strict defaults rakhta hai. (1) allowInsecureRequests: library http:// endpoints refuse karti hai; test server plain http://127.0.0.1 par chalta hai, toh yeh flag lagana pada. Production mein https hoga aur flag nahi chahiye. Yeh test environment ki baat hai, server ki nahi -- README mein caveat likha hai. (2) id_token_signed_response_alg: 'ES256': OIDC client metadata ka default id_token alg RS256 hai; hamara server sirf ES256 sign karta hai (discovery mein id_token_signing_alg_values_supported: ['ES256']). Client ko batana pada ki ES256 expect kare -- yeh correct client config hai. (3) Login form manual: openid-client client library hai, browser nahi; woh authorization URL banata hai aur callback process karta hai. Beech ka user interaction (form post with CSRF) test ka loginVia() karta hai: openid-client ka URL follow karo, hamara form post karo, redirect URL wapas do. Isse openid-client ka state, iss, PKCE aur id_token validation poora chalta hai.

Nonce failure debugging: openid-client ka message generic tha ('unexpected JWT claim value'); test ne wrapped oauth4webapi error ka cause check kiya ki '"nonce"' hi reject hua -- warna test kisi aur wajah se pass ho sakta tha.
why_needed: Interop failures aksar config mismatch hote hain; har setting ka 'kyun' pata hona chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Naye shehar mein gaadi chalana: wahan ke rules (left/right) maanne padte hain, gaadi kharab nahi hai.
how_it_works: discovery(issuer, client_id, { id_token_signed_response_alg: 'ES256' }, auth, { execute: [allowInsecureRequests] }).
in_this_project: test/interop.test.ts runOpenIdClientFlow, loginVia; src/server.ts discoveryDocument.
advantages: Strict library defaults ne humein honest rakha
disadvantages: Login form library se nahi chala
common_mistakes: allowInsecureRequests production mein chhod dena
Generic error message par test assert karna
follow_up_questions: Browser automation (Playwright) se full flow kab chahiye?
RS256 support add karna chahiye kya?

question: In stage 1, mutation M12 (audience check removed) did not turn the 'id_token presented as an access token' test red. What does that teach about defence in depth and about reading mutation results?
answer_hinglish:
M12 ne verifyJwt se aud check hata diya. Expect tha ki id_token ko /userinfo par bhejne wala test red ho, kyunki id_token ka aud client_id hai, access token audience nahi. Lekin woh green raha: verifyJwt typ ko pehle check karta hai, aur id_token ka typ 'JWT' hai, 'at+jwt' nahi -- toh 'unexpected typ' se reject ho gaya, aud check tak pahuncha hi nahi.

Seekh 1 -- defence in depth: ek attack (token confusion) ke liye do independent checks (typ aur aud) hain. Ek tode toh doosra bachata hai. Yeh achha hai.

Seekh 2 -- mutation results padhna: green test ka matlab 'mutation harmless' nahi; matlab us test ne specifically us rule ko isolate nahi kiya. Isliye ek dedicated test chahiye jo sirf aud tode: 'a correctly signed token with the wrong audience' (sahi typ, galat aud) -- woh M12 par red hua, saath mein unit test 'wrong audience -> JwtError'. Har security rule ka kam se kam ek test aisa ho jo sirf usi rule par fail ho.

Stage 2 mein same pattern: M18 ne write-ahead test ko side effect se red kiya (wo test M18 ke baare mein nahi tha) -- README yeh note karta hai taaki galat coverage claim na ho.
why_needed: Mutation testing ka value tabhi hai jab har red/green ko samjha jaaye.
real_world_analogy: Do taale ek darwaze par: ek tod ke check karo ki chor ruka -- ruka, lekin doosre taale ki wajah se. Pehle taale ka test alag karna padega.
how_it_works: verifyJwt order: alg -> typ -> kid -> signature -> iss -> aud -> exp.
in_this_project: src/jwt.ts verifyJwt; test/userinfo.test.ts; test/units.test.ts; README mutation tables (M12, M18 notes).
disadvantages: Har rule ke liye isolated test likhna extra kaam
common_mistakes: Green mutation ko 'koi farak nahi' bol dena
Side-effect red ko coverage maan lena
follow_up_questions: Equivalent mutant kya hota hai?
Kaunse rules ke liye abhi isolated test nahi hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Isolated tests zyada maintenance, lekin har rule ka independent saboot.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Refactor mein typ check hat jaaye aur aud test na ho -- token confusion wapas.
advanced.production_improvements: Har security rule ke saath 'isolated test' column README table mein.

question: M16 (apply-before-write) first went undetected. How would you design fault injection for disk writes so that durability-order bugs are always testable?
answer_hinglish:
Pehla write-ahead test store ko close karke write fail karwata tha. Bug: 'store is closed' check commit() ke shuru mein tha -- write aur apply dono se pehle -- toh apply/write ka order ulta karne se bhi throw apply se pehle hota tha. Test ne order nahi, sirf 'closed store throws' check kiya. Fix: check ko write step ke andar (durable()) rakha; ab mutation par apply pehle chalta hai aur memory badal jaati hai -> test red.

General lesson: fault ko bilkul usi operation ke andar inject karo jiske order ka test karna hai. Better designs: (1) Injectable writer: openFileStores ko ek optional write(fd, data) function do (default writeSync+fsyncSync); test ek writer de jo throw kare -- ab failure exactly disk write par hai, kisi precondition par nahi. (2) Fault after N writes: writer jo Nth call par throw kare, taaki multi-record requests (code grant 5 records) ka partial failure bhi test ho -- aaj ka 'fail closed' claim isi se verify hoga. (3) Crash simulation: log bytes ko arbitrary offset par truncate karke reopen (torn line test ka generalised version).

Yeh abhi implement nahi hai; aaj ka test durable() ke closed-check par tika hai. Interview mein M16 kahani yeh dikhati hai ki test 'pass' aur 'test sahi cheez test karta hai' alag baatein hain.
why_needed: Durability bugs normal tests mein kabhi nahi dikhte; unke liye deliberate fault injection chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Fire drill tab hi kaam ka hai jab aag ka alarm usi kamre mein bajaya jaaye jahan sprinkler test karna hai.
how_it_works: Today: closed store -> durable() throws -> apply not reached. Proposed: injectable writer / fail-after-N.
in_this_project: src/file-store.ts durable, commit; test/persistence.test.ts write-ahead test; README M16 note.
advantages: Mutation ne test ki kamzori pakdi
disadvantages: Partial multi-record failure abhi untested
common_mistakes: Precondition par fault inject karna
Ek baar green dekh ke mutation dobara na chalana
follow_up_questions: Fail-after-N writer se kaunsa naya bug mil sakta hai?
Jepsen-style testing kya hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Injectable I/O = better tests, cost: thoda API surface aur indirection.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Partial request failure (record 3 of 5) aaj test nahi -- claim 'fail closed' sirf reasoning se hai.
advanced.alternatives: OS-level fault injection (dm-flakey, LD_PRELOAD), CrashMonkey jaise tools.
advanced.production_improvements: Injectable writer + fail-after-N test suite, crash truncation fuzzing.

question: Mutation M29 (keys.json written with mode 0644) was caught by no test on Windows. Why, how was it finally verified, and what keeps it verified?
answer_hinglish:
keys.json private keys rakhta hai, isliye FileKeyRing.save() temp file ko openSync(tmp, 'w', 0o600) se banata hai (rename mode rakhta hai). Test 'keys.json is created with mode 0600 (owner only)' statSync mode & 0o777 === 0o600 check karta hai, lekin it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32') ke saath -- Windows par node mode ko lagbhag ignore karta hai (sirf read-only bit), toh assertion wahan meaningless hota.

Stage 2 ke mutation results pehle Windows machine par bane, toh M29 (0644) ne wahan 0 tests red kiye -- skipped test ko 'covered' bolna galat hota, isliye README mein gap ke roop mein likha gaya. Phir suite Linux (Ubuntu, Node 20) par chalaya gaya: saare 177 tests pass hue, mode test samet; 0644 likhne par mode test fail hua ('expected 420 to be 384', yani 0644 vs 0600), aur restore ke baad phir 177/177. README table ab '0 on Windows, 1 on Linux' kehta hai.

Verified rakhne ke liye: (1) CI matrix mein ek POSIX runner, warna agla regression phir sirf Windows par test hoga. (2) Windows ke liye alag control: directory par NTFS ACL -- code mein nahi, docs mein. (3) Optional: startup par permission check jo POSIX par galat mode dekh ke refuse kare. Lesson: platform-specific rules ko us platform par chalana padta hai jahan woh lagte hain.
why_needed: Skipped tests silent gaps hain; unhe track karna padta hai.
real_world_analogy: Smoke detector jo sirf doosri building mein lagta hai: is building mein test button dabane se kuch saabit nahi hota.
how_it_works: save: openSync(tmp, 'w', 0o600) -> write -> fsync -> rename. Test: statSync(...).mode & 0o777.
in_this_project: src/keys.ts FileKeyRing.save; test/keys.test.ts mode test (skipIf win32); README M29 row ('0 on Windows, 1 on Linux') aur note.
advantages: Gap honestly documented, phir Linux par verify hua
disadvantages: Windows par koi protection code se nahi
common_mistakes: Skipped test ko passing maan lena
Windows par chmod se protection expect karna
follow_up_questions: Windows ACL kaise script karoge?
CI matrix mein kaunse OS chahiye?

question: What is the difference between code coverage and mutation checks, and why did this project use hand-picked mutations M1-M40?
answer_hinglish:
Coverage batata hai ki kaunsi lines tests ke dauraan CHALI. Lekin ek line chal sakti hai bina kisi assertion ke uska result check kiye -- 100% coverage wala suite bhi ek toota rule pass kar sakta hai. Mutation check ulta sawaal poochta hai: agar main yeh rule tod doon, kya koi test fail hoga? Agar nahi, toh test us rule ko protect nahi karta.

Is project ka process: ek rule chuno (exact redirect match, PKCE check, write-ahead order, pre-publish key, logout URI exact match...), source mein jaan-boojh ke todo, poora suite chalao, red tests note karo, git checkout se restore, phir green confirm. Stage 1 ke M1-M15 haath se kiye; stage 2 ke M16-M40 ek script ne string replacement se kiye, vitest JSON reporter se failed tests gine.

Hand-picked kyun, Stryker jaisa tool kyun nahi? Security rules specific hain aur unhe naam se track karna tha (README table: rule -> tests). Tool hazaron random mutants banata jinme se zyada irrelevant. Findings: M8 (rotation test ne purana token try nahi kiya -- fix hua), M12 (typ check ne aud ko mask kiya -- dedicated test), M16 (write-ahead test order nahi dekh raha tha -- fix hua), M29 (Windows par skip; Linux par chala ke pakda gaya). Limit: sirf woh rules jo humne soche.
why_needed: Security code mein 'tests pass' ka matlab 'rules enforced' hona chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Coverage: guard ne har kamra ghooma. Mutation: ek khidki khuli chhodi, kya guard ne pakda?
how_it_works: Mutate -> run suite -> count failures -> restore -> table.
in_this_project: README mutation tables M1-M15 and M16-M40.
advantages: Har rule ka test se rishta documented
Weak tests mile aur fix hue
disadvantages: Manual chuna hua set; tool-level exhaustiveness nahi
common_mistakes: Coverage % ko quality maan lena
Mutation ke baad restore bhool jaana
follow_up_questions: Stryker ka 'survived mutant' kya hai?
Kitne mutations kaafi hain?

question: After a deploy, resource servers report 401 invalid_token 'unknown kid' from /userinfo for tokens issued just before. Walk through the investigation.
answer_hinglish:
'unknown kid' ka matlab: token header ka kid hamare ring.published(now) mein nahi hai. Possible causes is project mein: (1) Bina DATA_DIR deploy: StaticKeyRing har start par nayi generated key (ya SIGNING_KEY_FILE nahi diya) -- restart se pehle ke saare tokens unverifiable. index.ts ka 'listening' log line keySource ('generated' / 'file' / 'data-dir') aur kid dikhata hai -- pehle wahi dekho. (2) DATA_DIR naya/khaali directory (path badla, container volume mount nahi hua): FileKeyRing ne nayi keys.json banayi. 'store opened' log mein replayed: 0 iska hint hai. (3) keys.json restore/edit hua aur purani key hat gayi. (4) Clock: server ka clock aage jump hua toh retired key retention khatam samjhi gayi.

Verify: curl /jwks aur token ka header decode karke kid compare karo. Agar kid JWKS mein hai lekin phir bhi fail, toh woh 'unknown kid' nahi, 'bad signature' hoga -- alag problem.

Fix: DATA_DIR ko persistent volume par rakho, deploy checklist mein 'kid same rahe ya rotation planned ho'. Note: tokens 300 s ke hain, toh impact 5 minute ka; refresh tokens (opaque, store mein) agar store bacha hai toh clients refresh karke recover kar lenge.
why_needed: Key continuity deploys mein sabse aasaani se tootne wali cheez hai.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan ne raat ko taala badal diya aur purani chaabi waalon ko bataya nahi.
how_it_works: Token kid -> /jwks kids -> startup log keySource/kid/replayed.
in_this_project: src/index.ts startup logs; src/keys.ts FileKeyRing.open; src/jwt.ts verifyJwt ('unknown kid').
advantages: Startup logs mein kid aur key source
disadvantages: Koi automatic alert nahi
common_mistakes: Container ke andar ephemeral path par DATA_DIR
Har deploy par naya SIGNING_KEY_FILE
follow_up_questions: Deploy pipeline mein kid continuity check kaise jodoge?
Blue-green deploy mein keys kaise share hon?

question: Every token fails with 'wrong issuer' after moving the server behind a reverse proxy. What is the cause and the fix?
answer_hinglish:
Issuer identifier har token ke 'iss' claim mein hai aur verifyJwt use exact compare karta hai (opts.issuer = ctx.issuer). ctx.issuer ISSUER env se aata hai, default 'http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>'. Proxy ke peeche public URL kuch aur hai (https://auth.example.test), lekin agar ISSUER set nahi kiya, toh server internal URL ko issuer maanta hai. Tokens iss = internal URL ke saath bante hain, discovery mein endpoints internal URL ke hain, aur clients (jo public issuer expect karte hain) ya resource servers reject karte hain. Ulta bhi: agar ISSUER badla gaya toh pehle ke tokens (purane iss) 'wrong issuer' dete hain.

Yahi bug stage 2 ke restart test mein hua tha: naye random port par issuer badal jaata, toh test ne same port use kiya (startServer port option). Same root cause: issuer infrastructure se derive mat karo.

Fix: ISSUER ko public https URL par set karo (bina trailing slash -- createAuthHandler trailing slash par throw karta hai). https issuer par cookies Secure flag lete hain (secureCookie = issuer protocol https). Proxy ko HTTP par 127.0.0.1 tak forward karne do. Discovery check: curl /.well-known/openid-configuration -- 'issuer' public URL hona chahiye. openid-client discovery mein issuer mismatch par khud error deta hai.
why_needed: Issuer OIDC mein identity hai; galat issuer = poora trust chain toota.
real_world_analogy: Company ka letterhead purane address ke saath chhap gaya: har letter 'nakli' lagta hai.
how_it_works: ISSUER env -> ctx.issuer -> iss claim, discovery URLs, verifyJwt issuer, secureCookie.
in_this_project: src/index.ts ISSUER; src/server.ts createAuthHandler, discoveryDocument; src/jwt.ts verifyJwt; test/persistence.test.ts same-port restart.
disadvantages: Proxy headers (X-Forwarded-Host) se auto-detect nahi -- jaan-boojh ke
common_mistakes: Issuer ko Host header se banana (host header injection)
Issuer badal ke purane tokens expect karna
follow_up_questions: Issuer change ka migration plan kya hoga?
Kai domains ke liye ek server?

question: The server refuses to start with StoreCorruptError 'line N is not valid JSON'. What is your runbook?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh error readLog() deta hai jab store.jsonl ki koi COMPLETE line (jiske baad newline hai) JSON parse nahi hoti. Torn last line (crash mid-append) yeh error nahi deti -- woh chupchap drop hoti hai aur 'store opened' log mein droppedTornLine: true. Toh StoreCorruptError ka matlab beech mein kharabi: disk error, kisi ne file edit ki, do processes ne same file mein interleave karke likha (unsupported, koi lock nahi), ya file kisi aur cheez se overwrite hui.

Runbook: (1) Server band rakho; file ki copy lo (evidence). (2) Line N dekho: interleaving lagti hai (do JSON objects ek line mein)? Toh check karo ki do instances same DATA_DIR par toh nahi chale. (3) Option A: backup se restore. Option B: line N aur aage ko hata ke start karo -- lekin jaano kya kho raha hai: agar hatai hui lines mein code.used, refresh.used ya family.revoke the, toh restart ke baad woh codes/tokens phir 'unused/zinda' ho jaayenge -- security regression. Isliye safest option C: store.jsonl ko side mein rakh ke khaali store se start (sab users dobara login, saare refresh tokens invalid) -- fail closed. keys.json alag file hai, keys bachi rehti hain.

Kyun server khud guess nahi karta: mutation M20 (beech ki line skip) ka exact khatra yahi hai, aur test 'a bad line in the MIDDLE ... refuses to open' isko lock karta hai.
why_needed: Corrupt security state par 'best effort' recovery khatarnak hai; operator ko informed decision lena chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Bahi-khata ka beech ka page phata: andaaza lagane ki jagah audit karo, ya naya khata kholo.
how_it_works: readLog: split -> pop tail -> parse each complete line -> fail -> StoreCorruptError.
in_this_project: src/file-store.ts readLog, StoreCorruptError; test/persistence.test.ts corruption test; README crash safety.
disadvantages: Manual recovery, koi repair tool nahi
Checksums nahi, toh valid-JSON-but-wrong line nahi pakdi jaati
common_mistakes: Lines delete karke start karna bina samjhe kya kho raha hai
Do instances ek data dir par
follow_up_questions: Repair tool kaisa hona chahiye?
Backups ka RPO kya rakhoge?

question: Coding exercise: implement an RFC 7638 thumbprint for an EC P-256 public key using node:crypto, and write a test that recomputes it from the published JWK.
answer_hinglish:
Steps: (1) Public KeyObject ko JWK mein export karo: key.export({ format: 'jwk' }) -> { kty, crv, x, y }. (2) Required members lexicographic order mein: crv, kty, x, y. (3) Bina whitespace ke exact JSON string banao -- JSON.stringify(obj) par bharosa mat karo jab tak keys ka order aur extra members control na ho; template string sabse saaf. (4) SHA-256 over UTF-8 bytes, digest base64url. (5) Wahi kid JWK mein aur JWT header mein.

Test: server ka /jwks fetch karo, har JWK ke x, y se thumbprint recompute karo aur jwk.kid se compare karo; saath mein check karo ki 'd' (private part) undefined hai. discovery.test.ts mein yahi test hai. Bonus edge cases interviewer poochh sakta hai: RSA ke liye members e, kty, n hote hain; OKP (Ed25519) ke liye crv, kty, x. Agar kid thumbprint nahi hota (random string), toh file corruption (kid aur PEM mismatch) detect nahi hoti -- FileKeyRing.open isi par tika hai.
why_needed: Standard algorithms haath se likhna unki details samjhaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Fingerprint lena: ungliyon ka order fix hai, warna har baar alag fingerprint.
how_it_works: export jwk -> canonical string -> sha256 -> base64url.
in_this_project: src/jwt.ts jwkThumbprint, signingKeyFromPrivate; test/discovery.test.ts.
disadvantages: Sirf EC ke liye
common_mistakes: JSON.stringify(jwk) ka hash
base64 (padding) instead of base64url
follow_up_questions: RFC 7638 ka example vector kahan milega?
kid ko short kyun nahi karte?

question: Coding exercise: write a config validator for redirect URIs: absolute URL, http(s) only, no fragment, http only for loopback hosts. Then the runtime check.
answer_hinglish:
Config time validation (checkRedirectUri jaisa): (1) new URL(uri) -- throw ho toh 'not an absolute URL'. (2) u.hash ya uri.includes('#') -> reject (RFC 6749 3.1.2: redirection endpoint MUST NOT include a fragment). '#' ka extra check isliye ki 'https://x/cb#' mein URL parser hash ko '' de sakta hai. (3) protocol sirf 'https:' ya 'http:'. (4) http sirf hostname 127.0.0.1, [::1] ya localhost ke liye (RFC 8252 7.3 native apps / local dev). Galat config par start fail -- config error security bug hai, typo nahi.

Runtime check: client.redirect_uris.includes(requested) -- exact string. Koi normalisation nahi, kyunki normalisation (trailing slash, case, default port) hi bugs ka source hai. Mismatch par redirect mat karo; error page dikhao.

Tests likho: 'rejects a client with fragment / relative / http non-loopback' (units.test.ts) aur runtime 8 variants (authorize.test.ts). Same validator stage 2 mein post_logout_redirect_uris par bhi lagaya gaya.
why_needed: Config validation pehli defence line hai; runtime matching doosri.
real_world_analogy: Address book mein galat format ka address likhne hi na do; delivery ke waqt exact match.
how_it_works: URL parse -> fragment -> protocol -> loopback rule; runtime includes().
in_this_project: src/config.ts checkRedirectUri, validateConfig; src/server.ts redirectUriAllowed.
disadvantages: Custom URI schemes (native apps) support nahi
common_mistakes: Regex se URL validate karna
Runtime par normalise karna
follow_up_questions: Custom scheme redirect (com.example.app:/cb) kaise allow karoge?
localhost vs 127.0.0.1 ka RFC 8252 view?

question: Coding exercise: implement an in-memory refresh token store with rotation and family-wide reuse detection, storing only hashes.
answer_hinglish:
Data: families Map<id, {revoked}>, tokens Map<sha256(token), {familyId, used, expiresAt}>. issue(familyId): random 32 bytes base64url token, store hash, return raw token (sirf client ko). rotate(token): h = sha256(token); t = tokens.get(h); nahi mila -> 'invalid'; family revoked -> 'revoked'; expired -> 'expired'; t.used -> family revoke + 'reuse'; warna t.used = true (check-and-set synchronous, beech mein await nahi) aur naya token issue karo same family mein.

Key points jo interviewer dekhega: (1) Raw token kabhi store nahi -- DB leak se tokens nahi milte. (2) Mark-used aur issue ek synchronous section mein; database mein UPDATE ... WHERE used = false aur row count. (3) Reuse par sirf us token ko nahi, poori family ko revoke -- kyunki pata nahi kaun attacker hai. (4) Validation (scope, client) mark-used se pehle, taaki galat request token burn na kare. (5) Client binding: doosre client ka token -> error, revoke nahi.

Is project mein yahi logic MemoryTokenStore.markUsed + refreshGrant + reuseDetected mein bata hua hai; tests refresh.test.ts mein.
why_needed: Rotation + reuse detection interview mein common coding question hai.
real_world_analogy: Har baar naya bus pass, purana dikhaya toh poori family ke passes cancel.
how_it_works: hash -> lookup -> checks -> atomic mark -> issue new.
in_this_project: src/store.ts MemoryTokenStore; src/server.ts refreshGrant, reuseDetected; src/secrets.ts randomToken, sha256.
disadvantages: Grace window nahi
common_mistakes: Raw token store
Reuse par sirf ek token revoke
Async gap between check and set
follow_up_questions: Isko SQL mein kaise likhoge?
Family ki absolute lifetime kaise add karoge?

question: Coding exercise: write a vitest test that proves /logout refuses an unregistered post_logout_redirect_uri without any side effect.
answer_hinglish:
Test ka structure (logout.test.ts jaisa): (1) startServer() -- real HTTP server ephemeral port par. (2) login helper: getCode() se authorize + login form + code, phir redeem() se tokens; id_token, access token, refresh token aur session cookie nikaalo. (3) fetch /logout?id_token_hint=...&post_logout_redirect_uri=<galat>&state=x, redirect: 'manual' (warna fetch redirect follow kar lega aur 302 dikhega hi nahi). (4) Assert: status 400, Location header null (open redirect nahi), set-cookie null (cookie clear nahi hui). (5) Side effect check: access token se /userinfo abhi bhi 200 -- matlab family revoke nahi hui.

it.each se variants chalaao: prefix ('/logged-out/evil'), trailing slash, extra query, login ka redirect_uri (alag list hai), doosra host. Interview mein point: negative test sirf status code par nahi rukna chahiye; 'kuch nahi hua' bhi assert karo -- warna ek implementation jo pehle revoke karke phir 400 de, pass ho jaati. Mutation M30 (startsWith) is test ke prefix, slash aur query cases ko red karti hai.
why_needed: Security tests mein 'nothing happened' assert karna utna hi zaroori hai jitna error code.
real_world_analogy: Galat address par parcel: courier ne return kiya, aur parcel ka seal bhi nahi toota -- dono check karo.
how_it_works: login -> bad logout -> 400 + no Location + no Set-Cookie + userinfo 200.
in_this_project: test/logout.test.ts post_logout_redirect_uri %s test; test/helpers.ts getCode, redeem, userinfo.
disadvantages: Har case par naya login (thoda slow)
common_mistakes: redirect: 'manual' bhool jaana
Sirf status check
follow_up_questions: Isi test ko table-driven kaise banaoge?
Mutation se kaise verify karoge ki test kaam ka hai?

question: Coding exercise: implement rotate() for a key ring with next/active/retired states, retention, and persistence that rolls back on a failed save.
answer_hinglish:
State derive karo do timestamps se: activatedAt null -> next; activatedAt set, retiredAt null -> active; dono set -> retired. rotate(now): naya array banao (purana mutate mat karo, rollback ke liye): active ko retiredAt = now; pehli next ko activatedAt = now (agar next nahi mili -- hand-edited file -- toh nayi key bana ke directly active); phir ek naya next key generate karke add. Expired retired keys (now >= retiredAt + retainMs) filter karo. Phir save: JSON temp file mein mode 0600, fsync, rename. Save throw kare toh this.keys = before aur rethrow -- memory aur disk consistent.

published(now): non-expired keys, order active, next, retired. signing(now): age >= rotateAfterMs toh rotate, phir active key.

Interview checks: (1) Exactly ek active invariant (load time par bhi check). (2) Pre-publish: next key pehle se JWKS mein. (3) Retention = longest JWT lifetime, refresh tokens nahi (opaque). (4) Persist-before-effect ya rollback. (5) Clock injection for tests. Real code src/keys.ts mein; tests keys.test.ts (rotation, retention boundary, auto-rotation, persistence) aur mutations M23-M28.
why_needed: Key lifecycle state machine ka clean implementation senior coding rounds mein aata hai.
real_world_analogy: Shift change: naya guard pehle se gate par khada (next), shift badlte hi woh in-charge, purana kuch der saath rehta hai.
how_it_works: copy -> transform states -> add next -> prune -> save -> rollback on error.
in_this_project: src/keys.ts FileKeyRing.rotate, signing, published; test/keys.test.ts.
disadvantages: Single process only
common_mistakes: In-place mutation phir save fail
Next key ke bina rotation
follow_up_questions: Do rotations bahut jaldi ho toh kya guard?
KMS ke saath yeh kaisa dikhega?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Immutable copy = simple rollback, cost: thoda allocation (negligible).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Save ke baad crash: file nayi, memory gone -- restart par nayi state, consistent. Rename se pehle crash: purani file.
advanced.alternatives: KMS managed rotation; DB row with version + compare-and-swap for multi-instance.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Multi-instance: CAS on version, sirf ek winner rotate kare.
advanced.production_improvements: Rotation metrics, minimum gap, emergency remove.

question: Design: this authorization server must serve users in 10 regions with low latency. How do you split what is global and what is regional, starting from the current code's interfaces?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle current code ke pieces ko classify karo. (a) Stateless verification: access tokens ES256 JWT hain; koi bhi region JWKS se offline verify kar sakta hai -- yeh already global-friendly. (b) Signing keys: har region ko sign karna hai -> ya har region ki apni key (kid alag, JWKS sab regions ki keys publish kare), ya ek global KMS key (latency). Per-region keys + ek merged JWKS simple hai, aur rotation per region. (c) Strongly consistent state: code consume, refresh markUsed, family revoke -- yeh atomic hona chahiye. Codes 60 s ke aur usi region mein redeem hote hain jahan bane -> regional store theek. Refresh families: user ek region se doosre mein jaaye toh? Family ko home region par pin karo (token mein region prefix), refresh request home region par route ho. (d) Revocation (logout, reuse) global hona chahiye: family revoke home region mein authoritative, aur doosre regions /userinfo ke liye revocation events async replicate -- yahan eventual consistency ka window document karna padega. (e) Users aur clients config: read-mostly, globally replicated.

Current code se: CodeStore, TokenStore, SessionStore, KeyRing interfaces hi seams hain -- har region ka apna database-backed implementation, plus ek replication layer. Issuer: ek global issuer URL (GeoDNS/anycast) rakhna clients ke liye simple hai, kyunki iss sab tokens mein same hona chahiye. Kuch measure nahi hua; latency claims design assumptions hain.
why_needed: Global auth mein consistency (single-use, revocation) aur latency ka direct conflict hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank ki branches: cash har branch deti hai, lekin account freeze head office se sab branches tak jaata hai.
how_it_works: Global issuer + per-region signing keys in merged JWKS + regional stores + home-region families + replicated revocation.
in_this_project: src/store.ts interfaces (CodeStore, TokenStore, SessionStore); src/keys.ts KeyRing; src/server.ts handleUserinfo (revocation check).
advantages: Offline-verifiable tokens global scale ke liye natural
Interfaces migration ko local rakhte hain
disadvantages: Cross-region revocation eventual hai
Home-region routing complexity
common_mistakes: Ek global strongly-consistent DB har request ke liye (latency)
Har region alag issuer (clients confuse)
follow_up_questions: Region outage mein us region ki families ka kya?
Revocation replication lag kitna acceptable hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Regional atomic state + global async revocation: fast aur available, cost: revocation window. Global consensus: correct, cost: har refresh par cross-region latency.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Home region down: us region ke users refresh nahi kar payenge (fail closed) jab tak failover; replication lag mein revoked token doosre region ke /userinfo par chal sakta.
advanced.alternatives: Managed global IdP; CRDT-style revocation sets; short access tokens + introspection at home region.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10 regions: per-region key rotation, merged JWKS size chhota hi rahega (har region 2-3 keys). 100x users: DB sharding by family id.
advanced.production_improvements: Region-aware token format, revocation event bus, chaos tests for region failover, per-region SLOs measured.

question: Token introspection (RFC 7662) versus self-contained JWT access tokens: compare them for this server and say when you would switch or combine.
answer_hinglish:
Abhi: access tokens self-contained ES256 JWTs (5 min). Resource server JWKS se offline verify karta hai -- koi network call nahi, auth server down ho toh bhi verification chalti hai, scale aasaan. Cost: revocation dikhti nahi -- sirf hamara /userinfo jti -> family check karta hai; third-party API ke liye token exp tak valid. Token claims (scope, sub) leak bhi hote hain kyunki JWT readable hai.

Introspection: access token opaque ho, resource server har request par (ya cache ke saath) auth server ke /introspect ko poochhe 'active?'. Fayda: instant revocation, claims private, token chhota. Cost: har API call par network hop (ya cache jo revocation ko phir delay karta hai), auth server availability API availability ban jaati hai, aur introspect endpoint ko client authentication chahiye. Yeh PLAN stage 3 mein hai, bana nahi.

Combine kaise: (1) JWT rakho, plus introspection un APIs ke liye jo high-risk hain (payments) -- woh jti se revocation check karein. (2) Ya JWT lifetime aur chhota + introspection fallback. Switch kab: jab revocation SLA seconds mein chahiye aur API traffic auth server ki capacity mein ho, ya jab claims privacy zaroori ho. Is codebase mein jti -> family record pehle se hai, toh introspection ka data model ready hai; endpoint aur client auth reuse (authenticateClient) karna padega.
why_needed: Yeh senior interviews ka classic trade-off hai; dono ke failure modes jaanne chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Railway ticket par hologram (JWT) vs har station par TC central system se check kare (introspection).
how_it_works: JWT: verify locally. Introspection: POST /introspect token -> { active, scope, sub, exp } after family check.
in_this_project: src/server.ts sendTokens, handleUserinfo (jti family check), authenticateClient; PLAN.md stage 3 introspection.
disadvantages: JWT: delayed revocation
Introspection: latency + dependency
common_mistakes: JWT ko lamba (ghanton) rakhna aur revocation expect karna
Introspection bina caching ke high-traffic API par
follow_up_questions: Introspection response cache kitna safe hai?
Phantom token pattern kya hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Latency/availability vs revocation freshness ka direct trade.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Introspection: auth server down = APIs down. JWT: stolen token 300 s tak.
advanced.alternatives: Phantom token (gateway par introspect, andar JWT), DPoP sender-constraint, short JWT + push revocation.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Introspection 100x traffic par auth server ka sabse hot endpoint banega; caching aur horizontal scaling chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Introspection endpoint with client auth, jti deny-list for access tokens, metrics on token age at APIs.

question: To run two instances for high availability, someone proposes sticky sessions plus each instance keeping its own file store. Why is that wrong for this server, and what is the minimum correct design?
answer_hinglish:
Sticky sessions sirf browser requests ko ek instance par pin karte hain (cookie se). Lekin is server mein state browser ke bahar bhi travel karti hai: (1) Code /login par instance A par banta hai, lekin /token client ke BACKEND (confidential client) ya SPA ke fetch se aata hai -- woh sticky cookie nahi le jaata, toh B par 'missing code'. (2) Refresh token A ke store mein; client ka agla refresh B par jaaye toh invalid. (3) Revocation (reuse, /revoke, logout) sirf ek instance ke store mein -- doosre instance par wahi family zinda; reuse detection toot gaya kyunki B ne kabhi 'used' dekha hi nahi. (4) Signing keys alag hon toh JWKS mein dono instances ki keys chahiye; har instance sirf apni publish karega toh doosre ke tokens 'unknown kid'. (5) Instance A fail ho toh uske saare users ke refresh tokens gaye -- HA ka ulta.

Minimum correct design: ek shared, strongly consistent store (PostgreSQL) same interfaces ke peeche -- consume aur markUsed atomic UPDATE ... WHERE used = false; login transactions bhi shared (ya genuinely sticky, kyunki /authorize aur /login dono browser se aate hain -- yeh ek hi case hai jahan sticky kaam karta). Shared key ring (DB row ya KMS) jisme rotation ek jagah hoti hai, aur dono instances same JWKS publish karein. Health checks aur failover. README pehle hi kehta hai: file store ONE process per data dir.
why_needed: HA ka matlab sirf 'do copies' nahi; state ka ownership sahi hona chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Do cashier, har ek ka alag register: ek coupon dono par chal jaayega, aur ek bimaar pade toh uske customers ka hisaab gayab.
how_it_works: Shared store + shared key ring + stateless instances behind LB.
in_this_project: src/file-store.ts header comment (one process); src/store.ts interfaces; src/keys.ts KeyRing.
advantages: Shared store ke saath instances stateless aur replaceable
disadvantages: Database ek naya single point (uska HA chahiye)
common_mistakes: Sticky sessions ko distributed state ka hal samajhna
Har instance alag key
follow_up_questions: Database failover ke dauraan atomicity kaise bachegi?
Login transactions ko Redis mein rakhna theek hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Shared DB: correctness, cost: dependency aur latency. Per-instance state: simple, lekin galat.
advanced.failure_scenarios: DB replica lag par read replicas se refresh lookup: used token unused dikhega -- writes aur atomic reads primary par.
advanced.alternatives: Single active + hot standby with replicated log (simpler), ya managed IdP.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: connection pooling, read/write split carefully. 100x: sharding by family id.
advanced.production_improvements: PostgreSQL store + concurrency test (do redemptions ek saath do instances par), shared key ring, failover drills.

question: Plan a zero-downtime migration from the file store (store.jsonl) to PostgreSQL without losing single-use and revocation guarantees.
answer_hinglish:
Constraint: migration ke dauraan bhi ek code do baar redeem na ho, ek used refresh token dobara na chale, revoked family zinda na ho. File store single-process hai, toh 'dual write from two instances' jaisa kuch nahi; ek controlled cutover chahiye.

Plan: (1) PostgresStores implement karo same interfaces (CodeStore, TokenStore, SessionStore): tables codes(code_hash PK, ..., used, family_id, expires_at), families(id PK, sid, revoked, ...), refresh_tokens(token_hash PK, family_id, used, expires_at), access_tokens(jti PK, family_id, expires_at), sessions(sid PK, cookie_hash UNIQUE, ...); atomic UPDATE ... WHERE used = false. Poora existing test suite dono stores par chalao (stage 2 PLAN ka proof idea). (2) Importer: store.jsonl ko file-store ke apne readLog/apply se padho (same semantics), snapshot ko DB mein bulk insert. (3) Cutover: kyunki tokens 5 min ke aur codes 60 s ke, ek chhota write freeze acceptable ho sakta hai: server ko read-only/maintenance (503 on /token, /login) karo, final import, naye process ko DB ke saath start, freeze khatam. 'Zero downtime' strict chahiye toh: new server DB par, purana server proxy ban ke uske writes forward kare -- complexity zyada. (4) keys.json: alag; KeyRing ko bhi DB/KMS par le jaao ya file same rakho (single instance). (5) Rollback: freeze se pehle ki store.jsonl copy.

Honest: yeh design hai, koi migration code ya measurement nahi.
why_needed: Security state ki migration mein 'thoda data loss' bhi vulnerability ban sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank ka naya software: ek raat counter band, saare ledgers transfer, subah naya system -- beech mein koi transaction nahi.
how_it_works: Same interfaces -> dual test -> import via apply -> short freeze -> cutover -> rollback copy.
in_this_project: src/store.ts interfaces; src/file-store.ts readLog, apply, snapshot; PLAN.md stage 2 leftovers.
code_example:
-- the single-use guarantee in SQL
UPDATE codes SET used = true
 WHERE code_hash = $1 AND used = false
RETURNING client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, family_id;
advantages: Interfaces ki wajah se server.ts nahi badlega
disadvantages: Write freeze ya complex proxying
common_mistakes: Do systems mein ek saath writes bina coordination
Used flags import mein chhod dena
follow_up_questions: Freeze ka user impact kya hoga?
Migration ke baad dono stores ko compare kaise karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Short freeze simple aur safe; true zero downtime ke liye proxying ya dual-run complexity.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Import ke beech crash: idempotent import (PK conflicts ignore) se dobara chalao. Freeze ke dauraan clients 503 par retry karein.
advanced.alternatives: Log shipping: naya DB-backed process log tail kare jab tak cutover.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bade log par import time badhta hai -- compaction pehle karo (start par hoti hai).
advanced.production_improvements: Shadow mode reads, consistency checker, rehearsed cutover runbook.

question: Design the database indexes and retention rules for sessions, families, refresh tokens and access-token records, based on the queries this code actually makes.
answer_hinglish:
Queries code mein: getRefresh(token_hash), markUsed(token_hash) -> PK refresh_tokens(token_hash). getFamily(id), revokeFamily(id) -> PK families(id). familiesOfSession(sid) -> index families(sid) (memory store mein yeh linear scan hai; DB mein index zaroori). consume(code_hash), setFamily -> PK codes(code_hash). familyOfAccessToken(jti) -> PK access_tokens(jti). sessions.get(sid) -> PK sessions(sid); getByCookie(cookie_hash) -> UNIQUE index sessions(cookie_hash). Saare secrets ke columns hashes hain.

Retention (file store compaction ke rules se): codes expires_at ke baad delete (note: reuse signal kho jaata hai -- consciously); refresh_tokens expires_at ke baad; access_tokens expires_at ke baad (jti records ka expiresAt stage 2 mein isi liye add hua); sessions expires_at ke baad; families jab koi refresh token, access record ya code unhe refer na kare. DB mein yeh ek periodic DELETE job (batched) ya partitioning by expiry date (purane partitions drop -- sasta).

Hot paths: refresh_tokens par har refresh ek INSERT + ek UPDATE; access_tokens par har token ek INSERT. Revoked flag families par -- ek row update se poori family. Foreign keys refresh_tokens.family_id -> families.id useful, lekin cleanup order dhyan se.
why_needed: Indexes queries se nikalte hain, andaaze se nahi.
real_world_analogy: Library: book number se shelf (PK), author se alag catalogue (secondary index), aur purani magazines har mahine hatao (retention).
how_it_works: Map lookups in memory store -> PK/unique indexes; linear scan -> secondary index.
in_this_project: src/store.ts interfaces and Memory* classes; src/file-store.ts snapshot (retention rules).
disadvantages: Cleanup job ek aur moving part
common_mistakes: familiesOfSession bina index
Raw tokens ko column mein rakhna
follow_up_questions: Partitioning by expiry kab worth hai?
Cleanup aur active transactions ka lock contention?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Partitioning = sasta delete, cost: schema complexity. Batched DELETE = simple, cost: vacuum load.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Cleanup job ruk gaya: tables badhte hain, queries slow -- monitoring chahiye.
advanced.alternatives: Redis TTL keys codes ke liye; Postgres families ke liye.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x: refresh_tokens sabse bada table; hash-partition by family_id.
advanced.production_improvements: Cleanup metrics, table size alerts, retention policy doc.

question: A refresh request and a logout for the same session arrive at the same time. What are the possible outcomes in this server, and would they still hold with an async database store?
answer_hinglish:
Single process, sync stores: dono handlers async hain (body read await), lekin store operations synchronous hain aur har handler ke andar sequence mein chalti hain. Do orders: (A) Logout pehle store tak pahuncha: families revoked -> refresh request 'refresh token is revoked'. (B) Refresh pehle: markUsed true, naya refresh token aur access token issue (same family). Phir logout familiesOfSession(sid) -> wahi family revoke -> naye tokens bhi dead (same family). Dono orders mein end state: family revoked. Client ko B mein ek response tokens ke saath mila, lekin woh tokens 5 min se pehle /userinfo par 401 denge. Koi interleaving jahan refresh ke tokens 'bach' jaayein nahi hai, kyunki naye tokens nayi family mein nahi, usi family mein jaate hain.

Async DB store ke saath: sendTokens ke steps (markUsed, recordAccessToken, saveRefresh) alag statements ho sakte hain aur unke beech logout chal sakta. Kya end state phir bhi revoked? Haan, agar revoke family row par flag hai aur refresh/userinfo har baar family.revoked check karte hain -- naya refresh token row insert ho bhi jaaye toh agla refresh 'revoked' dekhega. Risk tab hai jab koi code path family check skip kare ya cache kare. Isliye invariant: 'har token use par family ka current revoked flag padho' -- yahi refreshGrant aur handleUserinfo karte hain.
why_needed: Concurrency bugs ko end-state invariants se reason karna aasaan hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ki chaabi bana rahe ho jab maalik ne taala badalne ko bola: nayi chaabi bhi purane taale ki hai, toh bekaar.
how_it_works: Revocation at family granularity + check on every use => order-independent end state.
in_this_project: src/server.ts refreshGrant, handleLogout, handleUserinfo; src/store.ts TokenFamily.revoked.
disadvantages: Client ko kabhi kabhi 'dead' tokens mil sakte hain
common_mistakes: Family revoked flag ko cache karna
Naye tokens ko nayi family mein daalna
follow_up_questions: Is race ka test kaise likhoge?
Logout ke response ke baad koi refresh success de sakta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Family-level flag cheap aur race-safe; fine-grained per-token revocation zyada state.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar resource server family state cache kare, revoked tokens cache TTL tak chalenge.
advanced.alternatives: Serializable transactions; version numbers on family.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Family row hot ho sakti hai agar ek family par bahut traffic (rare).
advanced.production_improvements: Concurrency tests with interleaving hooks; audit of all code paths that read family.

question: Where does this server spend CPU per request (scrypt, ECDSA sign/verify, SHA-256), how does each interact with Node's event loop, and what has been measured?
answer_hinglish:
Measured: kuch nahi -- README saaf kehta hai 'No performance numbers are claimed'. Lekin design se reasoning: (1) scrypt (login, confidential client auth, aur unknown user par dummy): node:crypto ka async scrypt libuv thread pool par chalta hai (default 4 threads), toh event loop block nahi hota, lekin 4 se zyada concurrent logins queue mein lagte hain; N=2^17 par har hash ke liye lagbhag 128 MiB memory bhi. Yeh sabse mehnga operation hona chahiye. Confidential client ke har /token aur /revoke par bhi scrypt chalta hai -- client secrets ke liye yeh mehnga hai (alternative: high-entropy client secrets ke liye fast hash ya private_key_jwt). (2) ECDSA P-256 sign (har token response mein 1-2 JWTs) aur verify (/userinfo, /logout): node:crypto ka sign/verify synchronous hai -- event loop par chalta hai. (3) SHA-256 (codes, tokens, safeEqual): chhota aur sync. (4) fsync (file store): sync, event loop block.

Measure kaise (PLAN stage 5): ek machine par per-endpoint latency distribution aur throughput, scrypt time per login, event loop lag metric (perf_hooks monitorEventLoopDelay) under load, thread pool size (UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE) badal ke. Raw results save karke, machine aur conditions ke saath. Tab hi koi number bolo.
why_needed: Bottlenecks guess karne ki jagah unhe event-loop model se samjho, phir measure karo.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant: tandoor (scrypt) 4 hi hain aur slow, counter (event loop) par sirf billing -- tandoor ki line counter ko nahi rokti, lekin bill printer (sync sign/fsync) rokta hai.
how_it_works: scrypt -> libuv pool (async). sign/verify/sha256/fsync -> main thread (sync).
in_this_project: src/secrets.ts scrypt wrapper, verifySecret, verifyAgainstDummy; src/jwt.ts signJwt, verifyJwt; src/file-store.ts durable; PLAN.md stage 5.
advantages: Async scrypt event loop ko free rakhta hai
disadvantages: Thread pool limit concurrency cap karta hai
Sync crypto aur fsync main thread par
common_mistakes: Sync scryptSync use karna
Benchmark ke bina scaling promise
follow_up_questions: UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE badhane ka downside?
Client secrets ke liye scrypt kyun overkill ho sakta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Strong password hashing = CPU/memory cost; yeh conscious security trade hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Login spike: thread pool saturated, logins slow; memory spike (128 MiB per concurrent hash).
advanced.alternatives: argon2id with tuned params, separate login service, rate limiting.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Horizontal scaling ke saath shared store; scrypt cost linear in logins.
advanced.production_improvements: Load test with saved raw results, event loop lag metric, per-endpoint histograms.

question: The project has zero runtime dependencies. What did that cost and what did it buy, specifically in stages 1 and 2?
answer_hinglish:
Runtime par sirf Node built-ins: node:http, node:crypto, node:fs. jose, openid-client, vitest, typescript sirf devDependencies hain (tests aur build).

Fayde: (1) Supply chain: koi transitive package auth server ke andar nahi chalta -- security-critical code ke liye bada plus. (2) Samajh: ES256 JWS format (ieee-p1363), RFC 7638 thumbprint, PKCE, scrypt params -- sab haath se, toh har detail interview mein samjhayi ja sakti hai. (3) Stage 2 persistence bina database ke: node:fs se append-only log, jo zero-dependency rule ki wajah se chuna gaya (PLAN ne PostgreSQL socha tha). 

Cost: (1) Correctness ka bojh humpar -- isliye interop tests zaroori the: jose aur openid-client independent judges hain ki hamara JWT aur protocol sahi hai. (2) Features jo libraries muft deti hain (RSA, JWE, many algs, form parsing edge cases) yahan nahi. (3) File store ki limitations (one process, no checksum) ek database se nahi aati. (4) Mutation checks aur bahut saare negative tests likhne pade.

Production ke liye honest view: ek real deployment mein audited libraries (jose) runtime par lena theek ho sakta hai; yeh project learning aur proof ke liye zero-dependency hai.
why_needed: Dependency decisions security aur maintainability dono par asar dalte hain.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ka furniture khud banana: har joint samajh aata hai, lekin har kursi ki jaanch khud karni padti hai.
how_it_works: Built-ins only at runtime; libraries as test oracles.
in_this_project: package.json (dependencies vs devDependencies); test/interop.test.ts; src/jwt.ts; src/file-store.ts.
disadvantages: Zyada code aur tests khud
Kam features
common_mistakes: Zero deps ko production ki best practice bol dena
Interop tests ke bina custom crypto
follow_up_questions: Kaunsi ek library aap production mein pehle add karoge?
devDependencies ka supply-chain risk?

question: Walk through how a request is routed and how errors are turned into responses in src/server.ts.
answer_hinglish:
createAuthHandler(opts) ek Ctx object banata hai: issuer, config (clients, users), ring (KeyRing), stores, now (injectable clock), lifetimes, audience, maxLoginFailures, secureCookie (issuer https hai?), dummyParams (pehle user ke scrypt params, taaki dummy hash ka cost same ho), failures map. Issuer trailing slash par throw karta hai.

Har request route(ctx, req, res) mein jaati hai: URL pathname par switch -- /.well-known/openid-configuration, /jwks, /authorize, /login, /token, /userinfo, /revoke, /logout, baaki 404 JSON. Har case allow([...methods]) se method check karta hai; galat method par 405 + Allow header. Har endpoint ka apna handler function hai (handleAuthorize, handleLogin, handleToken -> codeGrant/refreshGrant, handleUserinfo, handleRevoke, handleLogout).

Errors: handlers expected errors khud bhejte hain (oauthError JSON, sendHtml error page, bearerError). Unexpected exception route() ke promise se createAuthHandler ke .catch tak aati hai: agar headers bhej chuke toh socket destroy; HttpError (jaise body 413) -> oauthError with uska status; baaki sab -> 500 server_error 'internal error' (koi stack trace leak nahi). createAuthServer bas http.createServer(handler) hai; tests handler ko apne http.Server par lagate hain taaki ephemeral port pehle mile aur issuer usi se bane.
why_needed: Code ka structure samajhna har deeper question ki neev hai.
real_world_analogy: Reception desk: har visitor ko sahi counter par bhejo, galat time par aaye toh mana karo, aur koi bhi problem ho toh ek standard jawab.
how_it_works: createAuthHandler -> ctx -> (req,res) => route().catch(map errors). route: switch pathname -> allow -> handler.
in_this_project: src/server.ts createAuthHandler, route, createAuthServer; src/http.ts HttpError, oauthError; test/helpers.ts startServer.
disadvantages: server.ts lamba file hai (saare endpoints)
common_mistakes: Stack trace response mein
Method check bhool jaana
follow_up_questions: Isko alag files mein kaise todoge?
Request logging kahan add karoge?

question: What is a login transaction in this server, and how is it different from the stage 2 login session?
answer_hinglish:
LoginTransaction /authorize par banta hai jab request valid ho: { id, csrfToken, clientId, redirectUri, scope, state, nonce, codeChallenge, expiresAt (10 min) }. Yeh 'ek login attempt in progress' hai: validated authorization request server-side rakhi jaati hai taaki /login form ke saath client kuch badal na sake. Browser ke paas sirf auth_tx cookie (transaction id, Path=/login). Login success par transaction delete (single-use), 5 galat passwords par bhi delete, aur file store isse persist nahi karta.

LoginSession (stage 2) successful login ke BAAD banta hai: { sid, cookieHash, sub, authTime, expiresAt (12 h) }. Yeh 'user is browser mein login hua tha' record hai. Cookie auth_session (Path=/, random value, store mein hash), aur sid id_token mein jaata hai. Iska kaam abhi logout hai: session khatam karna aur uski token families revoke karna. SSO (bina form ke dobara login) abhi nahi hai.

Short mein: transaction login SE PEHLE (form ke liye), session login KE BAAD (logout ke liye). Dono ki cookies alag, lifetimes alag, aur dono HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax.
why_needed: Do similar-sounding concepts ko clearly alag karna beginner interviews mein common hai.
real_world_analogy: Transaction: bank counter ka token jab tak aapka kaam chal raha hai. Session: visitor register entry ki aap aaj aaye the.
how_it_works: authorize -> transaction + auth_tx cookie. login success -> transaction delete + session + auth_session cookie + code.sid.
in_this_project: src/store.ts LoginTransaction, LoginSession; src/server.ts handleAuthorize, handleLogin, txCookie, sessionCookieHeader.
disadvantages: Session abhi SSO ke liye use nahi hoti
common_mistakes: Transaction aur session ko ek cookie bana dena
Transaction ko reusable rakhna
follow_up_questions: SSO aane par session ka role kaise badlega?
Transaction ko persist kab karna chahiye?
